1. to set upright, erect , (Euripides):—;metaphorically to keep straight, set right , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to accomplish successfully, bring to a successful issue , (Plato Philosophus): —;Pass. to succeed, prosper , (Herdotus Historicus); δρᾶν κατώρθωσαι thou hast rightly purposed to do, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. intransitive as in Pass. to go on prosperously, succeed , (Thucydides); τὸ κατορθοῦν success ,…
a setting straight: successful accomplishment of a thing, success , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)
to bury in the earth , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν κατώρυξε buried head downwards, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)
Dep. to dance in triumph over, treat despitefully , Lat. insultare, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)
